title: IT Incident Triage: Database Outage
description: Diagnosing a high-latency connection and sudden failover alert in EU-West cloud cluster.
context: At 03:14 UTC, alert monitor reported API latency spiking from 45ms to 9800ms. PostgreSQL replica db-eu-2 reported replication lag exceeding 120 seconds. Primary db-eu-1 is responding to ICMP ping, but port 5432 is refusing connection pool handshakes due to max_connections exhaustion caused by an unindexed query storm from worker-node-04.
question: What is the primary root cause and recommended immediate action to recover the database service?

candidate_answers.text: Terminate runaway queries on worker-node-04 and temporarily throttle connection pool size while creating missing index.
Reboot the physical primary server host and re-route all writes to replica db-eu-2 immediately.
Increase max_connections parameter to 50,000 and restart PostgreSQL service.
Deploy a new VPC peering gateway and renew SSL certificates for EU-West.

verification_question: Does the selected action remediate connection starvation without causing split-brain replication data loss?

title: Customer Support: Billing & Subscription Tier
description: Deciding on tier upgrade dispute and prorated refund routing.
context: Customer enterprise account #4829 upgraded from Pro ($49/mo) to Enterprise Annual ($4,800/yr) 3 days ago. Their accounting department mistakenly executed a duplicate wire payment, and user permissions for SAML SSO are currently pending admin approval. Customer is asking for immediate reversal of the duplicate wire and provisioning confirmation for SSO.

Downgrade the account back to Pro tier and instruct customer to open a dispute with their bank.
Apply the duplicate wire as account credits for the next 10 years without refunding.
Close the ticket as resolved because subscription changes take 30 days to process.

title: Physics & Engineering: Thermodynamics
description: Thermodynamics problem on Carnot engine maximum theoretical efficiency.
context: An experimental thermal power plant operates using a heat reservoir at 800 Kelvin and discharges waste heat into a coolant reservoir at 400 Kelvin. The engineering team claims the current turbine prototype produces 320 kW of work from an input thermal energy of 500 kW.
question: According to the Second Law of Thermodynamics (Carnot limit), is this claimed efficiency achievable?

candidate_answers.text: No, because the Carnot limit is 50% (1 - 400/800 = 0.50), while the claimed prototype achieves 64% (320/500 = 0.64), violating thermodynamic limits.
Yes, because thermal cycle efficiency is always greater than 70% at temperatures exceeding 750 Kelvin.
Yes, provided the working fluid undergoes isobaric expansion rather than adiabatic expansion.
Insufficient data because enthalpy values for the specific coolant refrigerant were not provided.

verification_question: Is the violation of the Carnot efficiency limit scientifically verified?

title: Medical Triage Assessment
description: Evaluating urgent clinical presentation and determining priority acuity.
context: Patient is a 58-year-old male presenting with acute substernal chest pressure radiating to the left jaw and diaphoresis that started 40 minutes ago while at rest. Vitals: BP 168/98 mmHg, HR 102 bpm, SpO2 96% on room air. History of hypertension and smoking.
question: What is the recommended immediate clinical triage pathway?

candidate_answers.text: Immediate Emergency Department Level 1 triage, stat 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes, continuous cardiac monitoring, aspirin, and activate STEMI protocol if indicated.
Schedule an outpatient treadmill stress test for next week and prescribe antacids for gastroesophageal reflux.
Administer intramuscular antibiotics and discharge patient with oral hydration guidelines.
Recommend deep breathing exercises and follow up with primary care physician in 30 days.
